en: The Scripture on the Most Victorious Dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Imperial Subject Hōten, Daisō Daishi, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was dwelling in the Great Hall of the True Dharma within the Buddha-land of Sukhāvatī.
He sat down composedly.
At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitāyus addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara, saying:
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings—
those who are afflicted by illness, suffering,
and those with short lifespans— O son of good family.
This is the dhāraṇī dharma-gate of the most supreme uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.
If anyone receives, maintains, reads, and recites it,
they will swiftly attain freedom from illness, long life, and peace and happiness.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat,
joined his palms in reverent salutation,
and addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One."
"I now wish to hear this most supreme dhāraṇī dharma-gate of the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas;
it is well-vowed and well-expounded.
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the great assembly of devas and humans.
He entered the samādhi called "Universal Illumination and Auspiciousness.
Emerging from that meditative concentration,
he spoke this Dharma-gate of the Supreme Dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas, saying:
Oṃ namo bhagavate sarvatathāgatālokiteśvarāya buddhāya te | namaḥ tadyathā | oṃ bulong bulong ||
BHOḤ LOṢṬA LOṢṬA VILOṢṬA VILOṢṬA ASAMASAMANTAVĀŚA SAPARĀNĀGATI GAGANAŚABDAVIŚODHAYA ABHIṢIÑCATU MĀM SARVATATHĀGATA...
Āryatā sugatavaravakṣanā mṛdvī mahāmudrā-maṇḍalapadā āhara āhara āyusandhārani śodhaya śodhaya gaga...
Namo bhagavate uṣṇīṣāya vijayine pariśuddha-sahasarāśmi-saṃcodite sarvatathāgatāvalokiteśvara.
Āryāmitāparibhāṣaṇi sarvatathāgatamātṛdharṣaṇīpratiṣṭhitī sarvatathāgatahr̥dayādhiṣṭhita.
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ jvala jvala mahājvāla vajrakāya saṃhārana pariśodhaya sarvakarmavāraṇa vi...
Śūḍipratini-vardhaya vucchi śarvatathāgatasamayādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā oṃ muñca muñca mahāmuñca vi-
Munī munī mahāmunī mati mati mahāmati mama tuṣoti tathāgatabuddhakoṭipariśuddhiviśodhaya mṛtyu śodhaya hī hī jāya jāya vijāya.
Jaya jaya samāra samāra sphāraya sphāraya sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā śodhaya śodhaya moti vajriṇi vaḥ.
DHRĪḤ MAHĀVĪRI SVAVĪRI VAJRAGARBHI JAYA GARBI VIJAYA GARBI VAJRARUDRA GARBI.
VAJRA-DĀVA VAJRA-SAVAYA VARI-VĀṆI VAJRAPĀVA TU MAMA [insert name here] ŚARIRAṂ SARVA-SATTVA-ĀNĀGATA-PARITRĀYA.
Śrutivibodhamiśraṇa sarvagati-pariśuddhi-śāśvata-sarvatathāgata-śāśvataṃ samādhiṣyāmi muñca muñca siñca dhīḥ.
Dadya dadya vidadya vidadya muca muca vimuca vimuca sphuṭa sphuṭa visphuṭa visphuṭa samantamocaya samantaraśmiphaṭ.
Ṛṣṭi sarvatathāgatahrīṇaya dhiṣṭhāna dhiṣṭhitamudrā mudrā mahāmudrā maṇḍalapate.
*Svāhā*. O son of good family, this *dhāraṇī* gate of the supreme *uṣṇīṣa* of all Tathāgatas can extend one’s lifespan,
eliminate karmic offenses, and swiftly bring about purification.
If one writes this dhāraṇī dharma-gate upon plain silk or birch bark and places it within a stūpa,
performing extensive offerings, [the merit shall be immeasurable].
Having made these offerings, one should circumambulate [the object] a thousand times, paying respectful homage.
By making offerings according to one's means, one will obtain increased wisdom;
if one’s life span is seven days, it will be extended to seven years.
If their lifespan of seven years is extended to seventy years,
they shall obtain such long life, peace, and happiness, free from all diseases;
they shall attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives, clearly remembering them without forgetfulness.
If one wears it upon the crown of the head as previously described, the obstacles and karmic hindrances will be eliminated.
Furthermore, if one uses clean silk or birch bark to write this dhāraṇī along with one's own name and surname using bezoar, [the same result shall be attained].
Construct a stūpa out of sandalwood,
place this dhāraṇī within it inside a residence,
present extensive offerings, and circumambulate it one thousand times.
Recite this dhāraṇī eight hundred times;
it will eliminate all illnesses and extend one’s lifespan to a hundred years.
Furthermore, it is like having sandalwood where there was none before.
One should construct a stūpa using pure clay.
Inside, draw a *karmavajra*; on the outside, depict the guardians of the four gates of the Vajradhātu.
In the center, write one's own name and install the *dhāraṇī*.
The merit obtained will be no different from that previously described.
Alternatively, one may write this dhāraṇī using ox-gallstone (gorocanā) and place it inside a clean vessel, which is then covered with another clean vessel.
Within the temporary dwelling, perform extensive offerings so that one may long receive protection and be free from all calamities.
Furthermore, one should use cow dung that does not touch the ground.
Construct a square maṇḍala and scatter white flowers upon it.
Light four butter lamps and place them at the four corners of the altar.
Burn agarwood and milk incense;
fill a bowl with *argha* water,
and further fashion a garland using white flowers.
Place this dhāraṇī either within a stūpa, or within a merit-image, or upon the altar.
The practitioner shall press the altar with their left hand while holding a rosary in their right hand.
Recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times during the three periods of each day, consecrate three *liǎng* of water with it, and drink it yourself;
this will enable one to eliminate all illnesses and extend one's lifespan to a hundred years.
One will resolve all enmities and knots, attain a wondrous voice, and obtain unimpeded eloquence.
In every birth, one will constantly possess the supernormal power of recollecting past lives.
If one takes the previously consecrated pure water...
If one sprinkles [this water] upon the royal palace, one's own residence, and even the places where cattle, horses, and other animals dwell,
one will swiftly eliminate the calamities caused by rākṣasas, nāgas, and serpents,
and shall always receive protection.
One will be free from all fears.
If one has the suffering of illness, by sprinkling water upon the crown of the head,
all grave illnesses will be forever eliminated.
Thus, these immeasurable praises of the Great Dhāraṇī ensure that whatever one undertakes will certainly achieve fulfillment.
Furthermore, by taking a willow branch and empowering it twenty-one times with this dhāraṇī, one may use it to clean the teeth, thereby attaining freedom from illness, intelligence, and longevity.
Furthermore, use a clean vessel to hold water;
empower it twenty-one times.
Drink three *he* of this water three times each day.
Recite the empowerment once for each sip.
This will eliminate all illnesses and bring about peace, happiness, and long life.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara...
Having circumambulated the Buddha Amitāyus three times,
they joined their palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how do sons and daughters of good family..."
"I wish for you to explain the methods for accomplishing *homa* through the creation of Buddha images and their stūpas and temples.
The Buddha addressed the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Fearless One!
Listen attentively with a single mind; I shall explain to you that which you have asked.
At that time, the Tathāgata Amitāyus [spoke].
He also entered the samādhi called Universal Illumination Auspiciousness.
Emerging from that concentration,
he then spoke the dhāraṇī dharma-gate of the immeasurable life of all Tathāgatas, saying:
Oṃ amṛte amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavikrānti amṛtagame amṛtavarṇanirghoṣagaganakīrti kalisarvakīlaśaṅkaraṇakariye svāhā. When the Tathāgata Amitāyus had spoken this Dharma-gate, [he concluded].
He addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"If a son or daughter of good family uses this dharma-gate to empower and purify a buddha-field..."
Mixing the mud with water, perform further consecration.
Fashion the stūpa from the mud up to the *cakra* (the pinnacle),
consecrating each stage in succession and presenting offerings.
One will be able to attain vast and supreme benefits.
Furthermore, there is the method for the most excellent stūpas:
one may construct stūpas out of gold and silver, or stūpas out of lapis lazuli.
A stūpa made of padmarāga gems,
or even stūpas made of various other precious jewels,
should be adorned according to the ritual rules, twelve finger-widths in height, and placed upon a lotus pedestal.
On the four sides of the stūpa, one should place the Four World-Protecting Heavenly Kings (Lokapālas), holding banners in their hands.
In front of that stūpa, one should place Śakra, Lord of the Devas, holding a bow in his hand.
Furthermore, one should place the sons of the Śuddhāvāsa deities, holding incense, flowers, and ointments in their hands.
On the left side of the stupa, place the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
on the right, place the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Each holds a white lotus.
The ritual for the stūpa is thus.
Furthermore, one should separately draw a lotus flower and write this most supreme dhāraṇī of the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas around its perimeter.
Place it within the stupa.
Sprinkle it with scented water to purify it,
and present exquisite incense and flowers, making a thousandfold offering.
If one wishes to benefit all sentient beings,
prolonging their lifespans and increasing their wisdom,
one should always maintain purity and strictly observe the fast and precepts for a full day and night on the eighth day of the waxing moon.
Thereafter, recite this dhāraṇī one thousand times before the precious stūpa.
By doing so every month for six months, one shall obtain a lifespan of one thousand years;
or, if one maintains sincere devotion and diligence, reciting it day and night, one shall attain a long life of one hundred thousand (lakṣa) years.
If one constantly recites it daily, one’s lifespan will increase immeasurably;
one will possess great power, no different from that of devas, asuras, and others,
and will attain the merit of traveling freely through the air.
Furthermore, there is another ritual procedure: in a secluded place,
take pure earth and mix it with scented water to form clay for constructing a stūpa.
Whether one, two, three, four, five, or even up to a full hundred thousand times,
one should write this dhāraṇī at the beginning and place it within the stūpa,
performing hundreds of thousands of kinds of vast offerings.
Recite this dhāraṇī seven hundred times;
daily your wisdom will increase and your lifespan will be extended immeasurably.
Or, for the sake of all sentient beings who are bound by shackles and imprisoned, [recite it].
By reciting this dhāraṇī, one immediately attains liberation.
Furthermore, if there are sentient beings who increase their offerings before a stūpa of this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain liberation].
Recite and maintain this daily for eight hundred times,
giving rise to a mind of impartiality that benefits both oneself and others.
By practicing in accordance with the Dharma in this way, one will eliminate the eight hardships.
They shall always enjoy peace and happiness, live for a hundred years, and be beloved by all people;
before long, they will swiftly attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives.
At the end of their lives, such persons shall not be reborn in the miserable realms of hell, the animal kingdom, or the realm of Yama.
Just as a snake sheds its skin, they are immediately reborn in the Buddha-field of Sukhāvatī.
There they obtain great rewards and experience supreme, wondrous bliss that is beyond description;
furthermore, they shall never again hear the sounds of the hells.
How much more so for those who are born there!
At that time, the Tathāgata Amitāyus further explained the method for accomplishing the painted image.
May all sentient beings obtain immeasurable lifespan,
remain far removed from saṃsāra, and be liberated from all suffering.
First, use a pure young girl to prepare the thread.
Prepare a plain silk cloth of the prescribed dimensions and,
using excellent pigments, paint upon it the image of the supreme dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣa, together with its subtle characters, representing its meritorious qualities.
The image is to be installed within the stūpa;
its body emits a thousand rays of light and it sits upon a lotus and moon disc, adorned with all ornaments.
Its face is like the full moon, and the image has three faces, three eyes, and eight arms.
The right face has auspicious features and is golden in color;
the left face displays a wrathful expression with bared fangs and is the color of a blue lotus;
the central face is perfectly round and white.
The right hand at the heart holds a *karmavajra*;
the second hand holds a lotus upon which is Amitāyus Buddha;
the third hand holds an arrow.
The fourth hand performs the *varada-mudrā*.
The first left hand forms a vajra-fist holding a noose with the index finger extended upward;
the second hand holds a bow.
The third hand forms the mudrā of fearlessness;
the fourth hand holds a precious vase with a stūpa upon it,
and the syllable Oṃ is placed upon the neck.
Place the syllable A upon the heart;
place the syllable HŪṂ upon the forehead;
place the syllable TRAṂ upon the navel.
Having placed the syllable *Kṛ* upon the feet, recite *Oṃ arakṣa svāhā* for protection.
Having written one's own name beneath the mantra,
paint Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva on both sides of the image.
Holding a white fly-whisk in his hand,
above the face of the image, one should paint a deity from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens descending a rain of nectar;
this is to be done on all four sides of the hanging scroll.
Paint the wrathful deities Vajra-Acala, Cakrasaṃvara, Nīladaṇḍa, and Mahābala, each holding a sword,
a hook, a vajra, and a vajra-staff, causing the evil māras to be subdued.
Thus, one should paint the image on the scroll with a sincere mind.
When the practitioner performs this rite,
they must first, with a sincere mind, [pay homage] before a stūpa containing relics.
Having observed the fast and precepts with diligence for one day and night,
one should present a thousand kinds of offerings before the painted image,
beginning on the first day of the waxing moon.
Recite this dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*).
On the fifteenth day, again present a thousand kinds of offerings.
At dawn on the following morning, the sacred image of the dhāraṇī will manifest before you.
All that is sought shall be accomplished without exception.
Furthermore, one should install this dhāraṇī-paṭa image in a quiet and secluded place.
Sprinkle purified scented water and present it as an offering.
Recite this dhāraṇī eight hundred times every day.
Furthermore, on the first day of each month, present one thousand kinds of offerings.
If one recites this dhāraṇī one thousand times,
one will attain immeasurable lifespan, immeasurable majestic power, and the sovereign ability to soar through the air.
One will remember a thousand verses daily, and one's speech will never be erroneous.
It can remove all the grave illnesses of sentient beings.
If a person is unable to perform the ritual as previously described,
they may simply do so within their own dwelling.
On the eighth day of the waxing moon, sprinkle pure water to purify the area.
Install the painted image and make offerings according to one's means.
With a sincere mind before the image, recite this dhāraṇī seven hundred to eight hundred times.
If one recites this twenty-one times three times every day,
wisdom will increase, one will be free from illness and enjoy peace and happiness,
life will be extended to a hundred years, and the supernormal power of recollecting past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti*) will be attained.
If one is unable to perform the ritual and recitation oneself, it is likewise effective to request another to do so; this will result in longevity, intelligence, and wisdom.
Furthermore, the method of *homa* is for the purpose of benefiting sentient beings.
Construct a circular fire pit one cubit wide and twelve finger-breadths deep.
Encircle its exterior with a boundary of vajras and plaster it with a mixture of white sandalwood and white earth.
Use white flowers and scatter them within the incense burner.
Place four cups of ghee lamps at the four sides of the burner,
and immediately make offerings with fragrant flowers from all four directions.
Furthermore, set out an arghya vessel that is exquisite and prepared according to the ritual rules;
wrap a white cloth around the top of the vessel and place branches from flowering trees upon its mouth.
Regarding trees that have white sap:
take a green branch twelve finger-widths long and burn it together with dry firewood.
Immediately, he invokes the Fire Deity (Agni).
Having completed the invocation,
he pours three *śarāva* measures of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) into the hearth three times.
Recite the mantra of the Fire Deity (Agnideva) accordingly to empower it,
and then dispatch the Fire Deity.
Immediately visualize Amitāyus Buddha appearing clearly within the hearth.
Furthermore, recite the Uṣṇīṣa-agra-dhāraṇī-dharmaparyāya. Then,
as in the previous ritual procedure,
pour three *modaka* measures of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) into the hearth.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ amṛtodbhave svāhā. One should use the five grains;
take a pinch of grain with three fingers and dip it in ghee.
Recite the mantra once while voicing the specific wish you seek,
and cast it into the fire pit;
continue in this manner until eight hundred recitations have been completed.
The ritual procedure for the three sessions of the day is likewise.
Furthermore, recite the *Uṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī* of all Tathāgatas;
it wards off all diseases and bestows intelligence and long life.
Whatever one seeks shall be accomplished without fail.
Alternatively, on the eighth day of the lunar month,
perform the homa rite three times a day before the painted image.
Recite this mantra one thousand times.
Your lifespan will increase by a thousand years; you shall not harm sentient beings and shall constantly practice generosity.
By following such a ritual procedure, one can subdue enemies.
It increases wisdom and attains a wondrous voice.
If one cannot perform the rite oneself, one may request another to do so;
it will pacify and eliminate all evil calamities and afflictions.
Furthermore, regarding the method for accomplishment:
as before, perform the homa ritual using the five grains,
and recite the Uṣṇīṣa-agra-dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times.
Having performed the homa, one should further recite one lakṣa;
this can extend one's lifespan by one lakṣa,
reaching up to ten million years (koṭi) or even immeasurable years.
One may soar through the air with mastery and subdue demonic adversaries.
If one seeks wealth, nobility, or auspiciousness,
perform the homa ritual as previously described.
By reciting the dhāraṇī one lakṣa times, one will eternally attain great wealth and nobility.
If seeking an official position, by performing a homa with lotuses one lakṣa times, one will obtain a high-ranking office.
Furthermore, there is the accomplishment of the sword-rite (*khaḍga-sādhana*).
One should place the aforementioned painted image before a *śarīra* stūpa and present a thousandfold offering.
Recite this dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*).
Take five metals to fashion a sword and place it before the stūpa;
then, recite the dhāraṇī another hundred thousand times to empower the sword.
Having consecrated the sword,
he then grasped it with his right hand and attained the supernormal power of transformation with complete mastery.
Possessing great majestic power, they increase one's lifespan immeasurably and are able to bring about both calamity and fortune for all sentient beings.
Furthermore, there is another ritual procedure.
As before, by using the vajra, wheel, trident, and so forth,
one shall achieve accomplishment and obtain the aforementioned supreme and immeasurable merits.
This great dhāraṇī is the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas and is most rare;
whatever is performed according to the preceding instructions will certainly achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, if there should be another person...
Regarding this dhāraṇī dharma-gate of the most supreme uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas,
one should recite it twenty-one times during each of the three periods of the day;
having presented offerings, one should maintain it with a sincere mind and explain it for others.
May those sentient beings attain great happiness, long life, and freedom from illness;
may they possess great wisdom and obtain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives.
When those people pass away, like a snake shedding its skin, they shall immediately be reborn in the Buddha-field of Sukhāvatī and attain the great fruit of fruition.
They do not even hear the sounds of the hells and so forth,
let alone being born there.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra, [he sat in silence].
All those in the world—devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly delighted; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Most Victorious Dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas* as spoken by the Buddha.
